source_text:
Tit 2,7 Τὸ τῆς ἀδιαφορίας

ἐπὶ τοῦ νοῦ ἔλαβεν, τὸ δὲ τῆς σεμνότητος ἐπὶ τοῦ ἔργου, ἵνα μὴ μόνον ἔργου ἀπέχῃ
φθαρτοῦ ἀλλὰ καὶ νοήματος.
thought_title: Integrity of mind and dignity of work
orientation: Severianus is explaining Paul's instruction in Titus 2:7, distinguishing where integrity and dignity apply.
pass_a_gloss: Tit 2:7 The thing of integrity he took upon the mind, but the thing of dignity upon the work, in order that he may hold back not only from a corrupt work but also from a corrupt thought.

choices.why: Keeps the article-noun construction literal, matching the source's abstract phrasing without smoothing it into 'integrity' alone.
The verb means 'took' or 'received'; 'applied' would be interpretive, and the source says Paul took the quality upon the mind.
The subjunctive with ἵνα expresses purpose; 'hold back from' preserves the middle sense of keeping oneself away.
The adjective means perishable or corrupt; 'corrupt' fits the moral contrast with integrity and dignity.

bible_refs.note: Τὸ τῆς ἀδιαφορίας... τὸ δὲ τῆς σεμνότητος

pass_b_english: In Tit 2:7, Paul took integrity as a matter of the mind, and dignity as a matter of work, so that the teacher may refrain not only from corrupt work but also from corrupt thought.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'integrity' for ἀδιαφορία and 'dignity' for σεμνότητος, but ἀπέχῃ means 'abstain/keep away from,' not 'hold back.'
last_rejected.fix: so that he may abstain not only from corrupt work but also from corrupt thought.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀπέχω includes 'hold back from'; LSJ cites this sense. Within normal range, not a major error.

problems.quote: He took integrity as a matter of the mind, and dignity as a matter of work, so that he may hold back not only from corrupt work but also from corrupt thought.
problems.why: Subject of 'he may hold back' unclear; who is holding back? Titus? The teacher? Generic Christian?
Greek likely ἀφθορία (incorruption) or similar; 'integrity' may obscure physical/moral purity nuance needed for contrast with 'dignity'.

problems.quote: He took integrity as a matter of the mind
problems.why: 'He' could be Paul or Severianus; no antecedent in this section.

problems.quote: so that he may hold back not only from corrupt work but also from corrupt thought
problems.why: 'Hold back from' is awkward; the argument needs 'refrain from' or 'be kept from'.

edits.old: He took integrity as a matter of the mind, and dignity as a matter of work, so that he may hold back not only from corrupt work but also from corrupt thought.
edits.new: Paul took integrity as a matter of the mind, and dignity as a matter of work, so that the teacher may refrain not only from corrupt work but also from corrupt thought.

fixed: Subject of 'he may hold back' unclear: specified 'the teacher'.
'integrity' is the glossary-approved rendering for ἀδιαφορία; no change needed.
'He' replaced with 'Paul' to clarify the antecedent.
'hold back from' replaced with 'refrain from' for natural English.

problems.quote: Paul took integrity as a matter of the mind, and dignity as a matter of work
problems.why: No clear biblical basis given; seems to invent distinction without support.
problems.fix: Cite which Titus verse this comments on.
